title: The shift yesterday: was and were
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a falar sobre o passado com o verbo 'to be' nas formas was e were. Vai conseguir relatar como estava a produção, o turno ou a máquina no dia anterior — essencial para passagens de turno, relatórios de parada e conversas rápidas no chão de fábrica da Delta Ducon.
intro: On the shop floor, half of every conversation is about what happened. Was the line running? Were the filters clean? Was the team on time?
Today we practise was and were — the past of to be. With these two words you can describe a shift, a machine or a whole day at the plant.
introAudio: Hi, I am Marcos. Yesterday the night shift was calm and the machines were stable. Today we learn how to talk about the past with was and were.
vocab: The night shift was quiet at the Diadema plant.
The shop floor was busy during assembly.
The downtime was short on Monday.
The baghouse was ready for the inspection.
The scrubbers were online all afternoon.
The startup was smooth at the client site.
practice: The morning ______ was short one operator.
The ______ was clean and ready for work.
The machine ______ was only ten minutes.
The ______ was full of dust before cleaning.
The ______ was working well during the test.
The system ______ was planned for Friday.
The new ______ was delivered to Uberlândia.

audio.title: How was the shift?
audio.text: Yesterday was a good day on the shop floor. The morning shift was on time and the operators were ready at seven. The baghouse was clean and the scrubbers were online all day. There was only one short downtime after lunch. The maintenance team was fast, so we were back in production in ten minutes. The startup of the new line was smooth, and everyone was happy with the result.

readAloud: The shift was calm last night.
The operators were on time this morning.
The baghouse was clean before the inspection.
The scrubbers were online all day.
We were ready for the startup at eight.
fill: The filters ___ ready for the test.
qa: How was the shift yesterday?
It was calm and productive.
Were the operators on time?
Yes, they were on time.
Was the baghouse clean?
Yes, it was clean.
Were there any problems?
No, there were no problems.
How long was the downtime?
It was about ten minutes.

a.label: The shift was / The machine was

sentences: The shift was calm last night.
The operators were on time this morning.
The baghouse was clean before the inspection.
The scrubbers were online all day.
The downtime was short after lunch.
The technicians were at the client site.
The startup was smooth on Friday.
There were no problems on the shop floor.
grammarPoint: Was / Were são o passado do verbo to be. Use was com I, he, she, it. Use were com you, we, they. The shift was calm. — O turno estava calmo. The operators were ready. — Os operadores estavam prontos.
deepDive: Para negar, acrescente not: was not (wasn't), were not (weren't). Para perguntar, inverta: Was the shift calm? Were the filters clean? Dica prática: singular pede was, plural pede were.
examples: The baghouse was full of dust.
O filtro de manga estava cheio de pó.
We were at the client site.
The line was stopped for cleaning.
A linha estava parada para limpeza.
There were two technicians on the roof.
mistakes: No plural usamos were, não was.
No singular usamos was, não were.
A forma negativa é was not (wasn't).

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now report a full shift in the past — a skill every supervisor values.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você consegue relatar um turno inteiro no passado — uma habilidade que todo supervisor valoriza.

title: What we did last week: regular past verbs
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a formar o passado dos verbos regulares acrescentando -ed. Vai conseguir descrever ações concluídas na produção — o que a equipe instalou, testou, inspecionou e limpou — algo que você usa todos os dias em relatórios de manutenção e passagens de turno na Delta Ducon.
intro: Most of your work reports are lists of finished actions: we cleaned the ducts, we tested the fans, we checked the pressure.
In English, regular verbs show the past with -ed. Today we turn everyday plant actions into clear past sentences.
introAudio: Hi, I am Paula. Last week we installed a new fan and tested the whole line. Today we learn how to talk about finished work using verbs that end in e d.
vocab: We installed the new baghouse on Monday.
The team tested the scrubber before startup.
We inspected the ducts for leaks.
The operators cleaned the filter bags.
We replaced the worn valve last week.
The crew assembled the structure at the site.
practice: On Monday we ______ the new fan.
The team decided to ______ the scrubber again.
We need to ______ the ducts for leaks.
The operators had to ______ the filter bags.
We must ______ the worn valve today.
The crew came to ______ the structure.
Please ______ the pressure gauge before use.
They will ______ the old motor next week.

audio.title: Last week on the project
audio.text: Last week the team worked hard at the client site. We installed the new baghouse and connected the ducts. On Tuesday we tested the fans and checked the pressure. The operators cleaned the filter bags and inspected the seals. We replaced two old valves and assembled the support structure. Finally, we finished the job on Friday and the client thanked the whole crew.

readAloud: We installed the new baghouse on Monday.
The team tested the scrubber before startup.
The operators cleaned the filter bags.
We inspected the ducts for leaks.
The crew assembled the structure at the site.
qa: What did you install last week?
We installed a new baghouse.
Did the team test the scrubber?
Yes, they tested it twice.
Who cleaned the filter bags?
The operators cleaned them.
When did you finish the job?
We finished it on Friday.
What did you replace?
We replaced two old valves.
sentences: We installed the new baghouse on Monday.
The team tested the scrubber before startup.
The operators cleaned the filter bags.
We inspected the ducts for leaks.
We replaced two old valves last week.
The crew assembled the support structure.
They checked the pressure before startup.
We finished the job on Friday.
grammarPoint: Para o passado dos verbos regulares, acrescente -ed ao verbo. We install -> We installed. We test -> We tested. We installed the fan. — Nós instalamos o ventilador. The team tested the scrubber. — A equipe testou o lavador.
deepDive: Se o verbo já termina em -e, acrescente só -d: replace -> replaced. Se termina em consoante + y, troque por -ied: try -> tried. A pronúncia do -ed varia (t, d, id), mas a escrita é sempre -ed/-d.
examples: Nós instalamos o novo filtro de manga.
We finished the job on time.
Nós terminamos o serviço no prazo.
mistakes: No passado o verbo regular leva -ed.
Não dobre o -ed; use apenas uma vez.
Não dobre o n; clean -> cleaned.
We finish the job on Friday.
We finished the job on Friday.
A ação foi concluída no passado, use -ed.

celebrate.en: Excellent work. Regular past verbs unlock every maintenance report you will ever write in English.
celebrate.pt: Excelente trabalho. Os verbos regulares no passado destravam todo relatório de manutenção que você vai escrever em inglês.

title: Reporting problems: irregular verbs and did
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender os verbos irregulares no passado (go, take, break, see) e a fazer perguntas com did. Vai conseguir relatar o que deu errado e investigar causas — 'What happened? Did the fan stop?' — habilidade central em análises de falha e reuniões de manutenção na Delta Ducon.
intro: When something stops, everyone asks questions. What happened? Did the motor break? Where did the pressure go?
Many key verbs do not take -ed — they change completely. Today we learn these irregular forms and how to ask past questions with did.
introAudio: Hi, I am Diego. The fan stopped last night, so we went to the plant and found the problem. Today we learn irregular past verbs and how to ask questions with did.
vocab: We went to the site early in the morning.
The motor broke during the night shift.
We found a leak in the duct.
The operator saw smoke near the fan.
The line ran without problems all day.
practice: We had to ______ to the client site fast.
The old belt started to ______ under load.
The repair will ______ about two hours.
The technicians could not ______ the fault.
The scrubber did not ______ during the test.
We need to ______ back to the workshop.

audio.title: What happened last night
audio.text: Last night the fan broke during the second shift. The operator saw smoke and stopped the line. We went to the plant at once and found a burnt bearing. The repair took about three hours. Did the team have the right parts? Yes, they did. After the fix, the line ran again and the startup went well. We wrote a short report and sent it to the client.

readAloud: The motor broke during the night shift.
We went to the site early in the morning.
The repair took three hours.
The operator saw smoke near the fan.
Did the team find the problem?
fill: We ___ a leak in the duct. (find)
The line ___ well after the fix. (run)
qa: What happened last night?
The fan broke during the shift.
Did the operator see the problem?
Yes, he saw smoke near the fan.
How long did the repair take?
It took about three hours.
Where did you go?
We went to the client site.
Did the line run after the fix?
Yes, it ran without problems.
sentences: The motor broke during the night shift.
We went to the site early in the morning.
The repair took three hours.
The operator saw smoke near the fan.
We found a burnt bearing in the fan.
Did the team have the right parts?
The line ran well after the repair.
What happened to the pressure last night?
grammarPoint: Verbos irregulares mudam a forma no passado: go->went, break->broke, take->took, find->found, see->saw, run->ran. Para perguntar no passado, use did + verbo na forma base: Did the fan stop? — O ventilador parou?
deepDive: Atenção: depois de did o verbo volta à forma base, sem -ed e sem a forma irregular. Certo: Did the motor break? Errado: Did the motor broke? Na resposta curta: Yes, it did. / No, it did not.
examples: O motor quebrou ontem à noite.
We went to the client site.
We found a leak in the duct.
Nós encontramos um vazamento no duto.
The line ran well after the fix.
A linha funcionou bem após o conserto.
mistakes: Break é irregular: o passado é broke.
Go é irregular: o passado é went.
Depois de did o verbo fica na forma base.
Take é irregular: o passado é took.
Depois de did use see, não saw.

celebrate.en: Strong progress. You can now report a failure and investigate its cause in English — the heart of good maintenance.
celebrate.pt: Grande progresso. Agora você consegue relatar uma falha e investigar a causa em inglês — o coração de uma boa manutenção.

title: Safety instructions: do this, don't do that
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o imperativo para dar instruções diretas de segurança — 'Wear your helmet', 'Do not enter the area'. Vai conseguir orientar colegas e visitantes no chão de fábrica e entender placas e procedimentos, o que é vital para a cultura de segurança e a ISO 9001 na Delta Ducon.
intro: Safety talks the same way in every plant: short, clear commands. Wear your PPE. Check the pressure. Do not open the panel.
The imperative is the language of instructions and signs. Today we practise telling people what to do — and what not to do — on the shop floor.
introAudio: Hi, I am Sofia, safety coordinator. Before you enter the shop floor, wear your helmet and do not run. Today we learn how to give clear safety instructions in English.
vocab: Wear your helmet on the shop floor.
Put on your goggles near the scrubber.
Use gloves when you handle the filter bags.
Follow the lockout before any repair.
Read the warning sign at the entrance.
Press the emergency stop if you see danger.
practice: Always wear your ______ on the shop floor.
Put on your ______ near the grinding area.
Use ______ when you handle hot parts.
Follow the ______ before you open the panel.
Press the ______ if you see danger.
Do not remove your ______ near the machine.

audio.title: Before you start work
audio.text: Welcome to the shop floor. Before you start, put on your helmet, goggles and gloves. Read the warning signs at every entrance. Do not enter a marked area without permission. Follow the lockout procedure before any repair. Do not touch a running fan. If you see smoke or hear a strange noise, press the emergency stop and call the supervisor. Stay alert and keep the walkways clear.

readAloud: Wear your helmet on the shop floor.
Do not enter the area without permission.
Follow the lockout before any repair.
Do not touch a running fan.
Press the emergency stop if you see danger.
fill: ___ not run on the shop floor.
qa: What must I wear on the shop floor?
Wear your helmet, goggles and gloves.
Can I enter the marked area?
No, do not enter without permission.
What do I do before a repair?
Follow the lockout procedure.
What do I do if I see smoke?
Press the emergency stop and call the supervisor.
Can I touch a running fan?
No, do not touch a running fan.
sentences: Wear your helmet on the shop floor.
Put on your goggles near the grinder.
Use gloves when you handle hot parts.
Do not enter the area without permission.
Follow the lockout before any repair.
Do not touch a running fan.
Press the emergency stop if you see danger.
Keep the walkways clear at all times.
grammarPoint: O imperativo dá ordens e instruções. Use o verbo na forma base para dizer o que fazer: Wear your helmet. Para o negativo, use Do not (Don't) + verbo: Do not enter. Não usamos sujeito (nada de 'you'). Follow the lockout. — Siga o bloqueio.
deepDive: Don't é a forma curta de do not, comum em conversa. Em placas e procedimentos, prefira a forma completa Do not. Podemos suavizar com please: Please wear your gloves. O imperativo serve para instruções, avisos e passos de procedimento.
examples: Use luvas perto de peças quentes.
Do not touch the running fan.
Não toque no ventilador em funcionamento.
mistakes: No imperativo não usamos o sujeito you.
A ordem negativa precisa de Do not.
Depois de do not o verbo fica na base, sem -s.
Não use 'to' antes do verbo no imperativo.
O imperativo usa a forma base, sem -s.

celebrate.en: Great job. Clear safety instructions protect your team — and now you can give them in English.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Instruções claras de segurança protegem sua equipe — e agora você sabe dá-las em inglês.

title: Rules on site: have to, must and mustn't
grammar: have to / must / mustn't (obrigação e regras)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a expressar obrigação e regras com have to, must e mustn't. Vai conseguir explicar o que é obrigatório e o que é proibido em obra e comissionamento — 'You must sign the permit', 'You mustn't bypass a safety device' — essencial ao coordenar equipes e atender exigências de clientes e da ISO 9001 na Delta Ducon.
intro: Every project runs on rules. You must sign the work permit. You have to wear PPE. You mustn't bypass a safety device.
Have to, must and mustn't let you state obligations and prohibitions clearly. Today we use them to explain the rules of the plant and the job site.
introAudio: Hi, I am Rafael, site manager. On our projects you have to follow the schedule, and you must never bypass a safety device. Today we learn how to talk about rules with have to, must and mustn't.
vocab: You must sign the work permit first.
We have to follow the project schedule.
You must read the procedure before startup.
We have to meet the deadline for the client.
You mustn't bypass a safety device.
The team has to check every line during commissioning.
practice: You must sign the ______ before you start.
We have to follow the project ______.
You must read the ______ before startup.
We have to meet the ______ for the client.
The team checks every line during ______.
Everyone has to respect the ______ on site.

audio.title: Rules on our projects
audio.text: On our projects the rules are clear. You have to wear PPE at all times, and you must sign the work permit before you start. We have to follow the schedule, because the client has a strict deadline. During commissioning, the team must test every line and read each procedure. You mustn't bypass a safety device, and you mustn't work alone in a confined space. If you follow these rules, the startup goes safely and on time.

readAloud: You must sign the work permit first.
We have to follow the project schedule.
You must read the procedure before startup.
You mustn't bypass a safety device.
The team has to test every line.
fill: We ___ follow the schedule. (obrigação, have to)
The team ___ test every line. (has to)
You ___ work alone in a confined space.
He ___ wear PPE on site. (has to)
qa: What must I do before I start?
You must sign the work permit.
Do we have to follow the schedule?
Yes, we have to follow it.
Can I bypass a safety device?
No, you mustn't bypass it.
What does the team have to do during commissioning?
The team has to test every line.
Do I have to wear PPE?
Yes, you have to wear PPE at all times.
sentences: You must sign the work permit first.
We have to follow the project schedule.
You must read the procedure before startup.
We have to meet the deadline for the client.
You mustn't bypass a safety device.
You mustn't work alone in a confined space.
The team has to test every line during commissioning.
Everyone has to wear PPE on site.
grammarPoint: Must e have to expressam obrigação. Mustn't (must not) expressa proibição. You must sign the permit. — Você deve assinar a permissão. We have to follow the schedule. — Nós temos que seguir o cronograma. You mustn't bypass it. — Você não pode burlá-lo.
deepDive: Cuidado: mustn't é proibição (é errado fazer), mas don't have to é ausência de obrigação (não é necessário). Com he/she/it, have to vira has to: He has to wear PPE. Must não muda de forma: She must sign it.
examples: You must sign the work permit.
Você deve assinar a permissão de trabalho.
We have to follow the schedule.
Nós temos que seguir o cronograma.
We have to meet the deadline.
Nós temos que cumprir o prazo.
You mustn't bypass a safety device.
Você não pode burlar um dispositivo de segurança.
You mustn't work alone in a confined space.
Você não pode trabalhar sozinho em espaço confinado.
The team has to test every line.
A equipe tem que testar cada linha.
He has to wear PPE on site.
Ele tem que usar EPI na obra.
You don't have to stay after the shift.
Você não precisa ficar após o turno.
Everyone must respect the safety rules.
Todos devem respeitar as regras de segurança.
mistakes: You must to sign the permit.
Depois de must não se usa 'to'.
Depois de must o verbo fica na forma base.
A proibição é mustn't, não 'don't must'.
Depois de mustn't não se usa 'to'.

celebrate.en: Outstanding. You can now set clear rules and expectations in English — exactly what a strong industrial manager does.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você consegue definir regras e expectativas claras em inglês — exatamente o que um bom gestor industrial faz.
